thread:
jamie: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of mTLS handshake failures in eu-west-2 after the RBAC policy change this morning. ~10% of proxied ingresses returning 495/handshake-error. Anyone else?

kaya: saw the alert. I think the rotator job also got a role restriction at 09:12, might be related.

ops-bot: alert: proxy-mtls-handshake-failure rate > 5% for service=ingress-proxy-eu-west-2 (since 2026-03-21T09:18:02Z) :rotating_light:

jamie: exact failures from the proxy logs look like `client auth failed: no valid cert found` and `KMS decrypt failed: AccessDenied` in the rotator trace.

tia: if rotator can't unwrap the intermediate keystore, proxies will present an incomplete chain -> handshake fail. Did IAM role for rotator's service account get narrowed?

kaya: yes, PR #4523 tightened keystore access. It changed the role scope from `keystore:Decrypt` on `arn:aws:kms:*:keystore/*` to a more restrictive resource.

devin: copying log snippet from the rotator pod: 
```
2026-03-21T09:11:58Z rotator INFO loading keystore entry for service-x
2026-03-21T09:12:01Z rotator ERROR kms client decrypt: AccessDeniedException keyId=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-... requestId=xxx
2026-03-21T09:12:01Z rotator WARN falling back to cached certs (age=24h)
```

leo: fallback cached certs are old; proxies prefer chain building with current intermediates (we rotate roots every 12h). So fallback will cause handshake failure for a subset.

jamie: security-bot just flagged that audit logs for KMS Decrypt in eu-west-2 show no requester principal for a 2m window around 09:12. That's weird.

security-bot: audit anomaly: missing principal in CloudTrail entries for KMS.Decrypt operations in eu-west-2 between 2026-03-21T09:11:40Z and 2026-03-21T09:13:40Z. Investigating correlation with IAM role change.

kaya: possible timing window where role permission removed before new role allowance propagated. If the rotator had cached STS creds that got invalidated mid-op, CloudTrail may record the call with an empty principal.

tia: action plan: 1) rollback the RBAC tweak for the rotator to previous policy (kaya). 2) force a rotator restart to re-acquire creds (devin). 3) surface KMS Audit log evidence into S3 for forensics (leo). 4) add a temporary mitigation: allow proxy fallback to present full chain from previous keystore if decrypt fails twice within 30s (jamie).

kaya: rolling back PR now. ETA ~6m.

devin: restarting rotator deployment in eu-west-2: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore-rotator -n infra`

ops-bot: deploy event: keystore-rotator restart started for eu-west-2 cluster at 2026-03-21T09:20:05Z.

devin: rotator logs after restart: 
```
2026-03-21T09:21:10Z rotator INFO STS assume-role success (role=rotator-keystore-eu-west-2)
2026-03-21T09:21:11Z rotator INFO KMS decrypt succeeded keyId=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-... requestId=yyy
2026-03-21T09:21:11Z rotator INFO published new cert bundle service-x
```

jamie: handshake error rate dropped back to baseline ~0.3% after the restart and rollback. Good.

leo: pushed the relevant CloudTrail slice to S3 and kicked off the audit pipeline. Saved S3 path: `s3://redwood-audit/keystore/2026-03-21/eu-west-2/09-11-40_09-14-00.json`

security-bot: created incident INC-2026-031: `mtls-handshake-spike-eu-west-2` with severity=P2, assigned to @kaya and @devin.

kaya: root cause hypothesis: race between RBAC role update and rotator credential refresh leading to transient KMS decrypt failures and incomplete cert chains. Also: audit log schema doesn't consistently capture missing principal metadata in our ingestion path — we need to harden CT->audit pipeline.

tia: follow-ups to file as tickets: 
- ENGSEC-1221: Add pre-deploy canary for RBAC changes that exercise KMS Decrypt path (run rotator assume+decrypt).
- ENGSEC-1222: Make CloudTrail ingestion tolerant to missing principal fields and flag those events for manual review.
- ENGSEC-1223: Implement short-circuit in proxy to continue using last-known-good full chain up to 2x decrypt failures within 1m.

devin: quick vuln triage note: this isn't an exploit, it's a resilience gap. But if an attacker could flip role bindings they could cause DoS by breaking TLS — track as medium risk until mitigations.

jamie: agreed. Marking as security-advisory (internal) until post-mortem.

leo: i'll draft a short postmortem template and drop in #postmortems once we collect the audit slice and rollout timeline.

kaya: PR rollback merged. I'll add the canary check to our CI for RBAC patches.

jamie: thanks everyone. If anything else pops up ping here. :thumbsup:
